newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen stifled by holiday-thinned market.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen stifled by holiday-thinned market.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were practically inert through much of Wednesday's session as a holiday in Japan stifled market participation here.

Even newspaper reports quoting Takahiro Kawase, director of the Bank of Japan's policy planning department, saying the central bank would maintain its low interest rate policy for the time being failed to stir the Euroyen market, dealers said.
"There's nobody interested in Euroyen. At the end of the day, it's priced in no rate hikes until the summer," said a trader with a European futures house.
He said players were reluctant to push the back months higher since there was no guarantee rates would remain steady until September and beyond.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.29 at 1130 GMT against its IMM close at 99.30. Turnover was a meagre 1,315 lots.
Japanese government bond futures were not traded due to the Japanese holiday.
Eurodollar futures ended marginally firmer after a benign U.S. Consumer Price Index for December sparked an overnight rally in U.S. treasuries.
June Eurodollars finished at 94.20 against their IMM close at 94.19. September was at 94.03 against 94.01. Turnover for both months was a moderate 10,235 lots.
